body:
No objection was supplied in this round, so the live tension is between the account and the rival, and the rival has done most of the argumentative work. There is material worth taking and material worth pushing back on, and the two are separable.

Take first: the rival is right that the account's proposed remedy answers one reading among at least three, and that the material does not choose among them. The third reading — that the recurring argument is doing something other than failing to reach agreement, that the absence of a shared record is load-bearing rather than an accident of loose speech — is the one the account does least with, and nothing given refutes it. Keeping it live costs only the loss of a settled plan, which is a cost worth paying given how thin the evidence is.

Take second, and this is the part I would actually adopt now: the pre-record probe. Asking each flatmate separately what they thought a past agreement meant is cheap, and it discriminates. If later disagreements cluster around scope, or recurrence, or timing, the fix is narrower than a whole new system; if they don't cluster, the recording hypothesis loses ground. It has a second virtue the rival notes: it tests one-to-one talk with the avoidant friend without making the one-to-one approach the opening move. That sequencing is the real contribution here, and it is a revision of the account's order of operations, not of its contents.

Now the pushback, which matters because the rival oversells its case.

The account is not committed to the memory/recording reading alone. Its second conjecture already says the disagreement may be about what counts as done, on time, or fairly balanced — which is scope, recurrence and timing under other names — and its instruction to keep the vocabulary concrete (task, person, day, what 'done' means) is a response to exactly that ambiguity. So the rival's sharp dichotomy — reading one versus reading two, with the record answering only reading one — does not fit the text. The account's diagnosis is under-tested, not single-track. Similarly, the charge that the account 'treats a plausible diagnosis as if it were established' is too strong: the account marks the mechanism as conjecture, names a cheap falsifier, and lists what it does not know. That is not establishment. The rival's skepticism is welcome where it targets the unaddressed third reading; as a general charge it is unwarranted.

So my revision is narrower than the rival's. I would not drop the record and check-in; I would postpone them behind the probe. I accept that a note reading 'A: dishes, Mon' is not self-interpreting and can relocate the disagreement rather than settle it, but the account already asks for 'done' to be defined, which is most of the scope statement the rival wants. What is genuinely missing is recurrence: whether an offer is a one-off or a standing role. That belongs in the moment of agreement, spoken out loud, before anything is written.

On the avoidant friend, I accept the rival's criticism as a condition rather than a replacement. A private conversation can reproduce the outnumbered dynamic at smaller scale, so the reframing — 'I want your view of the group conversations' rather than 'why do you avoid them' — is worth adopting precisely because it is a proposal that inherits the uncertainty of the reading it depends on. Whether the friend re-engages then counts as evidence about the third reading, not merely about the success of the remedy.

Left open, and not to be papered over: which reading is right; whether the household wants any formalization; whether the avoidance predates the schedule changes; whether the disagreements are symmetric; and whether relocating the disagreement onto a record is an improvement or a delay. The material does not decide, and neither should I.

If asked what to do, my order is: run the probe separately with each flatmate, without adjudicating; read the answers for clustering; then choose among a record, a scope-and-recurrence practice, a group naming of the pattern, or nothing. Only the probe is something I would take up now. The rest is conditional on what it returns, and the rival's readings themselves are proposals about the flat, not findings.
commitments:
Taking this up involves a discriminating probe first, and everything else held conditional on what it returns.

The claim I am making about the texts, not about the flat, is that the rival mischaracterizes the account's diagnostic range: the account's second conjecture and its 'what done means' instruction already address scope ambiguity, so the rival's sharp split between a memory reading and a scope reading does not fit. That is checkable against the two artifacts, and I would drop it if the language there supports the rival's reading better than mine. Separately, I am treating all three readings as underdetermined by the material; that is a claim about the evidence, not about which reading is true.

The application I propose, and the only thing I would take up now, is the pre-record probe: ask each flatmate separately what they thought a past agreement meant, then read the answers for clustering around scope, recurrence or timing. Its relevance is discrimination among the readings; its weakness is that recollection is already the thing in dispute, so it returns reports, not facts, and may return nothing decisive. I commit to not treating non-clustering answers as support for whichever reading the asker already favored. Sequencing the probe before any written record, and testing one-to-one talk with the avoidant friend in that low-stakes form rather than as an opening move, depends on this proposal and inherits its uncertainty.

The reframed one-to-one conversation — 'I want your view of the group conversations' rather than 'why do you avoid them' — is a framing proposal I adopt as a condition on the account's approach, not as a replacement for it. It depends on the third, unaddressed reading, so if that reading is wrong the reframing may be solving a problem that isn't there. If the approach increases avoidance, that counts against my framing rather than being explained away as resistance.

On the record itself, I revise rather than reject: postpone it behind the probe, and add an explicit recurrence statement at the moment of agreement, since the account's 'what done means' covers scope but not whether an offer is a one-off or a standing role. I leave open whether a record relocates the disagreement rather than settling it, and whether relocation is an improvement or a delay.

Unresolved and not to be closed by me: no objection was supplied this round; the rival's third reading has its own move — naming the pattern in the group without assigning blame — that I have not tested and would not rank against the probe; and I still do not know whether any of this is about chores at all rather than something the chores express.
